name: Skimstinger
body:
Skimstinger
CR 3

This muscular, rust-and-yellow snake has bright, multifaceted eyes and hovers on wings resembling those of a dragonfly. A forked stinger hangs from its tail.

XP 800
N Small magical beast
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 16, flat-footed 13 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +2 natural, +1 size)
hp 32 (5d10+5)
Fort +5, Ref +8, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 60 ft. (perfect)
Melee bite +10 (1d4+1 plus dispelling bite) and sting +10 (1d3+1 plus poison)

STATISTICS

Str 13, Dex 19, Con 12, Int 1, Wis 12, Cha 5
Base Atk +5; CMB +5; CMD 20 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Dodge, Power Attack, Weapon Finesse Skills Fly +18, Perception +7, Stealth +12

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Dispelling Bite (Su)

A creature bitten by the skimstinger is affected as if targeted by a dispel magic spell with a caster level equal to the skimstinger’s Hit Dice (CL 5th for most skimstingers).

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 15; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d3 Str; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC includes a +2 racial bonus.

ECOLOGY

Environment any marshes
Organization solitary, flight (2-5), or hive (6-100)
Treasure incidental

Skimstingers are flying predators common to swamps, bearing both insect and ophidian features. While not particularly bright and posing only a moderate danger when encountered alone, these creatures are unfortunately far from solitary. Skimstingers almost always live in hives, constructed by hollowing out a great, dead tree. When the population of a particular hive exceeds the trunk’s capacity, skimstingers start to construct nests of sticks, saliva and wooden pulp on the sturdiest branches, of which each houses anywhere from one to five skimstingers. A skimstinger hive poses a terrible danger to its surroundings, especially since the creatures breed quite quickly if food is abundant enough. Such a group is often fearless and formidable enough to terrorize even the largest swamp predators.

Skimstingers fly about solitarily only as scouts and resource gatherers, and any creature that finds itself assailed by these flying snakes can expect more to show up expeditiously. Only scarcity of prey in the vicinity of the hive will drive single skimstingers to fly far enough that no backup will arrive when they find prey. In all other instances, a flight of skimstingers will fall upon the victim and harass it, biting and stinging until their potent poison saps all its strength and a true feast upon the helpless being’s still living body can begin in earnest. Besides their weakening poison, skimstingers have a meager arsenal, as their relatively small size limits the damage they can inflict, and so they rely on their toxin and numbers to do the heavy lifting in combat. The creatures are relentless when they attack, and their superior aerial mobility means they are very hard to get rid of once they start their assault.

It is unknown how the skimstingers came into being, and while their appearance and abilities hints at their beginnings as an artificial creation, there are little records of wizards or alchemists laying claim to these foul creatures, and none at all of those who could provide any proof of that. Their antimagic bite is possibly the strangest part of their arsenal, and one that is the hardest to explain evolutionarily or theologically. Swamp creatures bolstering themselves with magic are scarce, and it hardly fits any deity’s portfolio. Most proponents of the “created skimstinger” theory postulate that the creatures were specifically designed as a counter to wizards and other spellcasters, striking fast and in great numbers, shattering their magical defenses and injecting into their bodies a poison that would make quick work of their most likely feeble bodies. Newly settled skimstinger hives are often correctly identified as a great danger by nearby lizardfolk, who quickly mount assaults aimed at eradicating the creatures before they breed. Occasionally beast handlers, shamans or druids of the tribe may capture and train some stragglers left after such raids, taking great care to capture only males or females, as only the most powerful magic could be expected to keep a domestic hive in check.

Skimstingers are about 4 feet in length and weigh just under 10 pounds, though their bodies are highly muscular. Sexual dimorphism is readily apparent in the species. Females are larger than males and boast bright colors, mainly on the yellow-orange spectrum. They also possess the poison-injecting stingers, which males lack. Males, besides being smaller and lacking stingers, are easily recognizable by their muted green color.

To create a male skimstinger, reduce Str and Con by 2 and remove the sting natural attack. This reduces the creature’s CR by 1.

This unicorn seems larger and even more majestic than others of its kind. It displays its horn proudly, its radiance almost blinding.
